review_notes: I read the whole 68-line file. I did not search the wider sources. The only repetition is inside `solution`. Its two `rcases hd ... with h2 | h2` branches both rewrite with `h1`, take the coefficient at 1, simplify, and cast back from `O'` to `ℤ`. That is about four routine lines per branch. The two helper lemmas `coeff_one_sub` and `coeff_one_add` are short `simp only` computations that differ in sign. The rubric excludes short calculations, routine unfolding and moving duplicated branches into a helper. It also asks for nontrivial reasoning repeated across at least two proofs, and here the repetition is within one proof. A shared lemma would save little and would not make the proof easier to read or maintain. I found no justified finding. I did not check whether other files in the repository repeat this argument.
